craft_notes: Sthāyin: śānta of landing — rest, fulfillment, no-other-standing; autonomy dawning mid-proof. Inseparable pair kept whole (distinct-and-indistinct); no experience outside it. Rejected: (a) resolving the pair → killed: the pair IS the term (bhinnābhinna-viniścaya). (b) stands→is → killed: sthā-verbs carry standing-doctrine. Read aloud: a-PART from dis-TINCT-and-IN-dis-TINCT … WHOSE-self IS-un-GRASP-ing.

lines: Apart from distinct-and-indistinct assurance, no experience stands —
none apart from linked shining, whose self is ungrasping.
l4.sanskrit_cite: na caivānubhavo 'py asti bhinnābhinnaviniścayam muktvānvayasya prakāśasya vimarśarahitātmanaḥ

reads_against.argmap: Is there experience without grasp? → Experience just is grasping certainty; grasp-less shining experiences nothing.
c1_essence: What never stood cannot stand another: consciousness fits itself to this and I, orders inert selves by double certainty, and completes severed grasping in self-rest (vv10-15).
The same self twofold — breath-bound atom, unbroken whole — gathers in one continuous end-ground where nothing shows more inert than shining (vv16-18).
